Nutrition and Rheumatoid Arthritis
Th e role of diet and nutritional supplements in the etiology 
and treatment of RA has been a topic of considerable interest 
and speculation for decades. However, studying the relation-
ship between diet and RA is problematic given the multiple
risk factors for RA, the episodic nature of RA symptoms, the
expense of conducting long-term randomized controlled trials, 
the diﬃ  culty of measuring diet, and the diﬃ  culty of assessing
subjects’ compliance to dietary change.56
Th ere is evidence that lower intakes of vegetables, fruits, and 
dietary vitamin C are associated with increased risk of develop-
ing RA. It has been observed that there is a lower risk of devel-
